newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE leader tells U.S. he's worried by Iran build-up.
newsitem.headline: UAE leader tells U.S. he's worried by Iran build-up.

text.p: The president of the United Arab Emirates expressed deep concern about Iran's military build-up in the Gulf during two hours of talks with U.S. Defence Seretary William Cohen on Tuesday, a senior American defence official said.

Cohen stopped in the UAE briefly on a Gulf trip and held discussions on issues ranging from Iran to the stalled Middle East peace process and U.S. jet fighter sales with Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan at the president's home in Abu Dhabi.
"They (UAE officials) are very nervous about the Iranian build-up," U.S. defence department spokesman Ken Bacon told reporters after the talks.

"His (Sheikh Zaid's) feeling obviously is that they (Iran) are doing this for a reason. He talked about their arms build-up, he talked specifically about their efforts to develop weapons of mass destruction. He did not talk specifically about what he thinks is going to result, but he is quite concerned about it," Bacon said.
The talks came only hours after Cohen at a news conference in Bahrain said Iran had conducted two successful tests this month of a new air-launched anti-ship cruise missile obtained from China.
Tehran has also bought three submarines from Russia and is steadily obtaining other military equipment, according to Washington.

The UAE and Iran are in dispute over the sovereignty of three islands -- Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunbs -- in the southern Gulf near the narrow mouth of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran currently holds the islands.
Bacon said that Sheikh Zaid had "expressed discomfort and concern about the amount of money they (Iran) are putting into building up their military".
The Pentagon spokesman also said Cohen and the UAE president discussed the stalled Middle East peace process and that Sheikh Zaid told the secretary both sides had to make compromises.

"He said the U.S. and other countries interested in brokering peace in the Middle East have to figure out a way to get the peace process going again, that this was extremely important for stability in the area," Bacon said.
Sheikh Zaid, speaking very calmly, did not blame one side or the other for the derailed process and did not link Iran as trying to interfere with Middle East peace, Bacon said.
Cohen and Sheikh Zaid briefly discussed the UAE's consideration of an offer by the United States to sell as many as 80 F-16 fighter jets to the emirates.
But Bacon said there was no decision and that the UAE was still looking at the planes.
